Actions: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) laid out guidance for raising the federal funds rate off the zero lower bound and for tapering asset purchases.
FOMC statement introduced language that inflation was due to “transitory factors.”
FOMC removed “transitory” language from the statement.

Date: The Committee accelerated pace of tapering and signaled the tapering pace would likely mean the end of purchases in March 2022.

Actions: FOMC statement indicated that the Committee expected it would soon raise the target range.

Date: Fed released Principles for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve’s Balance Sheet.
FOMC lifted the target range from the effective lower bound.

Actions: FOMC released detailed plans for significantly reducing the size of the Fed’s balance sheet (consistent with January Principles).
Fed began reducing its holdings of securities.
10 rate hikes varying in size from 25 to 75 basis points.

Date: The target range moved from 0 to 0.25 percent to 5.0 to 5.25 percent.
